blocks.prompt: 7 Given the function \[f(x) = \begin{cases} 2x + 3, & x \le 1 \\ -x + 4, & x > 1 \end{cases}\]Discuss the limit and continuity at \(x = 1\).
blocks.explanation:
A limit-and-continuity question for a two-piece function.
We must say whether \(\lim_{x \to 1} f(x)\) exists and whether \(f\) is continuous at \(x = 1\).
Plan: find \(f(1)\), the LHL and the RHL, then apply the criterion and the three conditions.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = 2x + 3\) for \(x \le 1\), \(-x + 4\) for \(x > 1\).
To find: the limit and the continuity of \(f\) at \(x = 1\).
Method: \(f\) is continuous at \(x = c\) when three conditions hold: (i) \(f(c)\) is defined, (ii) \(\lim_{x \to c} f(x)\) exists (LHL = RHL), (iii) \(\lim_{x \to c} f(x) = f(c)\). If any one fails, \(f\) is discontinuous at \(c\).

Condition (i): find \(f(1)\)
\[f(1) = 2(1) + 3 = 5\]
Why: \(x \le 1\) includes 1, so the first piece gives \(f(1)\).

Left hand limit
\[\lim_{x \to 1^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 1^-} (2x + 3)\]
\[= 2 + 3 = 5\]
Why: Left of 1 the first piece is used.

Right hand limit
\[\lim_{x \to 1^+} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 1^+} (-x + 4)\]
\[= -1 + 4 = 3\]
Why: Right of 1 the second piece is used.

Condition (ii): does the limit exist?
\[\text{LHL} = 5\]
\[\text{RHL} = 3\]
\[5 \ne 3\]
Why: The one-sided limits differ, so \(\lim_{x \to 1} f(x)\) does not exist.

Conclusion
Condition (ii) fails, so \(f\) is discontinuous at \(x = 1\).
Why: One failed condition is enough. The graph jumps from height 5 (left) down to height 3 (right).

Check
\[f(0.99) = 1.98 + 3 = 4.98\]
\[f(1.01) = -1.01 + 4 = 2.99\]
Why: The two sides settle near different numbers, 5 and 3.
blocks.final_answer: LHL \(= 5\), RHL \(= 3\): \(\lim_{x \to 1} f(x)\) does not exist, so \(f\) is discontinuous at \(x = 1\)
